messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Increased DNS resolution errors + intermittent TCP resets for services routed through Azure northeurope expressroute peer. Affected: Private deployments with on-prem egress. Pager: oncall-amber. Incident channel created. Incident ID: INC-1912345678 :rotating_light:

maya: seeing spikes in DNS NXDOMAINs from our edge resolver for rdw-infra-prod services in northeurope. rates up ~15% last 5m.

josh: confirmed from customer VPN side — traceroute shows traffic reaches azure vnet but drops after first hop. attaching output:
```
traceroute to 10.10.5.1 (10.10.5.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  192.168.1.1 (192.168.1.1)  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.5 ms
 2  10.200.0.1 (10.200.0.1)  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  168.63.129.16 (168.63.129.16)  5.2 ms  5.1 ms  5.0 ms
 4  * * *
```

netops-lead: looks like egress path oscillation — BGP withdraws observed from MSFT side. checking bgp session logs.

sre-jen: DNS logs show upstream resolver timeouts to 168.63.129.16 and occasional SERVFAILs. lowering DNS TTL to 30s for affected records to speed failover.

oncall-amber: paging now. I'm going to notify customers with active private deployments in NEU. drafting message to CS.

customer-success: please include recommended mitigation for customers: failover to secondary region (westeurope) + switch routing to backup expressroute circuit.

josh: also seeing ICMP unreachable from MSFT routers then come back — possible control plane instability. opened ticket with Azure support SR# 123456789.

incident-bot: Azure Health: Partial Outage impacting "Azure Virtual Network / ExpressRoute" in northeurope — link: https://status.azure.com/en-us/status/northeurope #attached

maya: mitigation plan: 1) Reduce DNS TTL to 30s (done), 2) Advertise backup on-prem route via alternate circuit, 3) Route traffic to westeurope for critical customers using our smart-routing policy.

netops-lead: initiating BGP pref change to prefer backup AS path for customers A and B. monitoring.

sre-jen: adding temporary retry/backoff in gateway proxies to avoid cascading 502s (patch rolling).

oncall-amber: handoff at 08:00UTC to josh; I'll stay on call until 07:50UTC for questions. logging notes in incident tracker.

josh: Azure support says they are investigating "control plane churn". They requested packet captures and BGP logs — uploaded to SR.

customer-success: emailed affected customers with status and recommended temporary failover. two customers requested help performing BGP pref change — assigned to netops-lead.

maya: observed error rates drop to 3% after pref change and DNS TTL adjust. still seeing occasional blips.

incident-bot: update recorded: mitigations applied, impact reduced to P2. Please continue monitoring. :white_check_mark:

oncall-amber: handing off to josh. Summary: DNS upstream timeouts + BGP withdraws in northeurope causing intermittent egress failures for Private customers; applied TTL reduction, BGP pref to backup, proxy retries; Azure investigating. Keep incident open until Azure confirms fix.

josh: acknowledged. will escalate if reappears. scheduling postmortem: 24h window. anyone want to add action items?

netops-lead: action items: collect BGP timestamps and correlations with Azure health events; automate failover playbook for expressroute egress; add synthetic checks per customer circuit.

sre-jen: add logging alert for SERVFAIL rate >5% for 5m.

customer-success: update sent to customers with 60m cadence until resolved.

deploy-bot: rolling patch for gateway proxy initiated across 3 zones — 1/3 complete.

maya: still seeing one customer with persistent fails — opening dedicated thread with CS and netops offline.

josh: Azure updated SR: "Routing fabric instability - we are rolling fix to control plane" ETA 45m.

incident-bot: final: last recorded operator action at 1912345950. Closing note will be added after postmortem. :spiral_calendar:
